title: Amca Wins First Enterprise Wide Army Deal for Missile Components
summary:
A new partnership between the US Army and Amca will focus on the rapid qualification and manufacturing of hardware for critical military defense systems. The enterprise-wide contract with Army Materiel Command is the first of its kind and aims to increase the readiness of a priority missile system by re-engineering subsystems to improve their manufacturability.

The initiative targets the modernization of decades-old parts that face obsolescence and shrinking industrial capacity. Amca uses an AI-native component design platform and eight US certified factories to address long lead times and missing engineering data. Jai Malik of Amca noted that the difficulty of qualifying a single component can now rival the time once needed to build a complete aircraft.

Amca has been awarded a contract by the @USArmy, establishing an enterprise-wide partnership with Army Materiel Command for rapid engineering, qualification, and component production.

This is the first partnership of its kind, designed to increase readiness for a priority missile system by re-engineering and improving manufacturability of critical components and subsystems.

We're grateful for the Army’s trust, urgency, and leadership, and look forward to re-engineering American industry together.

Pleased to share that we've won an enterprise-wide Army contract to modernize decades-old components.

Over the past two years, our team has built the tech and muscle to re-engineer the parts our planes, ships, and tanks depend on and make them a lot easier to manufacture.   

We have also seen firsthand what America lost by trading hardware engineering for legal and financial engineering.  Qualifying a single component can now take as long as building an entire aircraft once did.

Our country simply can't afford this reality anymore. Our partnership here is the first step toward restoring America's engineering strength across its critical supply chains. More to come soon...
